response.title: which power stations still charge in freezing weather
response.answer:
Some portable power stations can charge below freezing (32°F / 0°C), but most standard LiFePO₄ models cannot unless they have a battery-heating system.

The key distinction is between:

Operating in freezing weather: Many power stations can discharge down to −4°F (−20°C).

Charging in freezing weather: Most stop accepting a charge below 32°F (0°C) to protect their batteries.

Charging with self-heating: Certain models warm their battery cells first, then accept AC, solar, or vehicle charging.

If you're using a power station outdoors in winter, look for automatic battery heating, not just a low operating-temperature rating.
